clusters.name: ARFID (DSM p.376)
items: Avoidant or restrictive eating leading to persistent failure to meet nutritional/energy needs (DSM p.376)
Significant weight loss or failure to achieve expected growth in children (DSM p.376)
Significant nutritional deficiency (DSM p.376)
Dependence on enteral feeding or oral nutritional supplements (DSM p.376)
Marked interference with psychosocial functioning (DSM p.377)
Absence of body image disturbance or body weight/shape concern (DSM p.377)

clusters.name: Pica (DSM p.371)
items: Persistent eating of nonnutritive, nonfood substances for >=1 month (DSM p.371)
Developmentally inappropriate (recommended minimum age >=2 years) (DSM p.371, p.372)
Not culturally or socially normative (DSM p.371)

clusters.name: Rumination Disorder (DSM p.374)
items: Repeated regurgitation of food for >=1 month (DSM p.374)
Food may be re-chewed, re-swallowed, or spit out without nausea or disgust (DSM p.374)
Not attributable to an associated gastrointestinal condition (e.g. GERD, pyloric stenosis) (DSM p.374)

criteria.thresholds: Pica & Rumination: >=1 month (DSM p.371, p.374); ARFID: persistent failure to meet nutritional needs (DSM p.376)
subtypes: ARFID - Lack of Interest in Eating/Food (Dulcan p.415)
ARFID - Fear of Aversive Consequences (Dulcan p.415)

epidemiology.prevalence: ARFID: 0.3% community (DSM p.377), similar to AN in pediatric clinics (Dulcan p.417); Pica: 1.6-5% school children (DSM p.372), 28% pregnant women (DSM p.373); Rumination: 1.5-5.1% primary school (Dulcan p.417)
epidemiology.sex_ratio: ARFID: 1:1 overall, male predominance with comorbid ASD (DSM p.378); Pica: equal in children (DSM p.373)
epidemiology.onset_age_typical: ARFID: Infancy/early childhood (sensory/interest) or any age (aversive event) (DSM p.377); Pica: Early childhood (DSM p.372); Rumination: 3-12 months in infants (DSM p.375)
epidemiology.prognosis: ARFID: chronic if untreated (DSM p.377); Rumination in infants: often spontaneous remission but can be fatal if severe (DSM p.375)

etiology.genetic: Family history of anxiety disorders and maternal eating disorders in ARFID (DSM p.378)
etiology.neurobiology: ARFID: 3D model - gustatory/insula sensory processing, hypothalamic/ghrelin appetite regulation, amygdala fear conditioning (Dulcan p.419). Pica & Rumination: CSTC dorsal habit loop (Dorsal Striatum to OFC) (StahlNeuro p.539, p.540)
etiology.environmental: Pica/Rumination: neglect, lack of stimulation, psychosocial stress, maternal feeding interaction (DSM p.372, p.375, p.377)

first_line: CBT-AR (Cognitive-Behavioral Therapy for ARFID, 4 stages) (Dulcan p.430)
Habit Reversal Training (HRT) + Diaphragmatic Breathing for Rumination (Dulcan pp.430-431)
Habit Reversal Training (HRT) for Pica (Dulcan p.431)
second_line: Olanzapine off-label for severe ARFID with anxiety/weight gain need (Dulcan p.428)
Mirtazapine / Cyproheptadine for appetite stimulation in ARFID (Dulcan p.428)
SSRIs (Fluoxetine, Sertraline) for comorbid anxiety/OCD (Dulcan p.428)
key_side_effects: Olanzapine: weight gain, metabolic syndrome, sedation (StahlKids pp.351-360)
SSRIs: activation, disinhibition, suicidal ideation risk (StahlKids p.201)
Stimulants warning: appetite suppression exacerbates ARFID (Dulcan p.418)
treatment.monitoring: Weight, height/growth velocity, nutritional status, metabolic panel for SGA (fasting glucose, lipids) (Dulcan p.423; StahlKids p.353)

items: PARDI (Pica, ARFID, and Rumination Disorder Interview) for ages 10-22 (Dulcan p.424)
NIAS (Nine Item ARFID Screen) with 3 subscales (Dulcan p.424)
EDY-Q (Eating Disorders in Youth-Questionnaire) for primary school children (Dulcan p.424)
Ch-EDE (Child Eating Disorder Examination) to differentiate ARFID from AN (Dulcan p.424)
ESP (Eating Disorder Screen for Primary Care) 5-question screener (Dulcan p.612)
Celiac disease, IBD (Crohn's, UC), GERD, Achalasia (Dulcan p.423)
Tonsillar hypertrophy and swallowing neuromuscular disorders (DSM p.379; Dulcan p.423)
PANS/PANDAS with acute food restriction (DSM p.379; Dulcan p.371)
Anorexia Nervosa (distinguished by body image disturbance) (DSM p.379)
Pica complications: lead poisoning, bowel obstruction/bezoar, parasitic infection (DSM p.372; Dulcan p.421)
Rumination mimics: GERD, Pyloric stenosis, Gastroparesis, Sandifer syndrome (DSM p.375)
key_numbers: Minimum age 2 years for Pica to rule out developmental mouthing (DSM p.372)
Minimum duration >=1 month for Pica and Rumination (DSM p.371, p.374)

high_yield: ARFID is distinguished from AN/BN by the complete ABSENCE of body image disturbance and fear of weight gain (DSM p.377; Dulcan p.415)
Pica diagnosis requires a minimum age of 2 years to rule out normal developmental mouthing in infants (DSM p.372; Dulcan p.416)
Rumination is an un-forced regurgitation without nausea/disgust, effectively treated with Habit Reversal Training and Diaphragmatic Breathing (Dulcan pp.430-431)
Stimulants for comorbid ADHD (present in ~24% of ARFID) must be used with extreme caution due to appetite suppression exacerbating ARFID (Dulcan p.418)
Acute onset of extreme food restriction in children should raise suspicion for PANS/PANDAS (DSM p.379; Dulcan p.371)
CBT-AR Stage 1 focuses on early volume increase in underweight patients or variety expansion in normal weight patients (Dulcan p.430)
